simple: This page shows how to animate UI smoothly using tweens. A tween slides a property from where it is now to a new value over time, so a menu can glide in, a button can grow, or a health bar can shrink gently instead of jumping. You use `TweenService` with a `TweenInfo` that says how long and in what style. It also shows how to chain tweens and how to make text appear letter by letter like a typewriter.
analogy: A tween is like a flipbook. You draw the first and last pictures, and the computer draws all the in-between pages so the motion looks smooth.
keyPoints: Tweening fills in the in-between steps so a UI change looks smooth instead of instant.
The pattern is: make a `TweenInfo`, call `TweenService:Create(object, tweenInfo, { Property = target })`, then call `:Play()`.
You can tween `Position`, `Size`, `Rotation`, transparency, and color properties; set `AnchorPoint` first so it moves or spins around the right spot.
Use scale values in `UDim2` targets so the result looks right on every screen size.
Put UI in a `CanvasGroup` and tween `GroupTransparency` or `GroupColor3` to fade or tint everything at once.
Put several properties in the same table to tween them together, like position and rotation.
Start the next tween when the previous one's `Completed` event fires to make a sequence.
`EasingStyle` (like Linear, Quad, Back, Bounce, Elastic) sets the feel; `EasingDirection` (In, Out, InOut) sets where the easing happens. The defaults are Quad and Out.

terms.tween: Short for "in-between". An animation that smoothly changes a value from start to finish.
terms.TweenService: The Roblox service that creates tweens.
terms.TweenInfo: Settings for a tween, like how long it takes. `TweenInfo.new(2)` means 2 seconds.
terms.interpolation: Calculating the values in between. Going from 0 to 10, halfway would be 5.
terms.easing: How the speed changes during the tween. Out starts fast and slows down at the end.
terms.Back / Bounce / Elastic: Fun easing styles that overshoot and settle, bounce at the end, or wobble like a rubber band.
terms.CanvasGroup: A frame that can fade or tint everything inside it as one.
terms.Completed: An event that fires when a tween finishes.
terms.MaxVisibleGraphemes: How many characters of a text label are shown. Raising it by 1 each step makes a typewriter effect.
terms.grapheme: One visible character, like a letter or an emoji.

example.title: Slide a menu in from the left, then wiggle it
example.place: LocalScript inside a Frame named Menu (inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
example.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local menu = script.Parent

-- Start off-screen to the left
menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
menu.Position = UDim2.fromScale(-0.5, 0.5)

-- 0.6 seconds, overshoot a little then settle
local slideInfo = TweenInfo.new(0.6, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local slideIn = TweenService:Create(menu, slideInfo, { Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5) })

-- A short tilt after it arrives
local tiltInfo = TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, 1, true)
local tilt = TweenService:Create(menu, tiltInfo, { Rotation = 5 })

slideIn.Completed:Connect(function()
	tilt:Play() -- start the wiggle when the slide finishes
end)

task.wait(1)
slideIn:Play()
explain: We set the menu's `AnchorPoint` to its center and put it off-screen to the left (X scale -0.5).
We make a tween that moves it to the screen center in 0.6 seconds with `Back` easing, so it overshoots a bit and settles.
We make a second tween that tilts it 5 degrees, repeats once, and reverses, so it tilts and comes back.
When the slide's `Completed` event fires, we play the tilt.
After waiting 1 second, we start the slide.

watchOut: Creating a tween does nothing until you call `:Play()`.
Tweening `Position` with pixel offsets can end up off-center on other screens. Use scale values.
If an object spins around its corner instead of its middle, set `AnchorPoint` to (0.5, 0.5).
Do not tween the `Thickness` of a `UIStroke` on text; it can cause lag and flicker.
Two tweens changing the same property at the same time will fight. Chain them with `Completed` instead.
